newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila eyes control on imported sugar supply.
newsitem.headline: Manila eyes control on imported sugar supply.

text.p: The Philippines' Sugar Regulatory Administration (SRA) said on Monday it would seek to expand its authority including the power to seize imported sugar in the local market in order to check surplus supplies.
"Our idea is to avoid a situation where sugar imports destroy the equilibrium of market forces," SRA chief Wilson Gamboa said in a statement.
Gamboa told Reuters it was one of the recommendations to be presented by the Presidential Task Force on Sugar to President Fidel Ramos by the middle of the year.
Gamboa said the proposal included a provision that the SRA be allowed to seize legally imported sugar as well. He did not say how it would be possible.
The task force was created to study different strategies to revive the domestic sugar industry which has been suffering from a sugar glut caused by massive imports last year.
At present, there is a surplus of about one million tonnes of sugar in the market which has dampened domestic prices squeezing profit margins of sugar producers.
The expanded authority would also allow it to force traders to sell their stocks in the market in case of extreme shortage, Gamboa added.

"Our (present) mandate does not carry any power. We have gotten the blame for almost everything primarily the release of imported sugar into the domestic market. The reality is we cannot even lift a finger to intervene," he said.

Gamboa said the measure is not inconsistent with the principle of free trade. "Even under the World Trade Organisation, there is still room to allow protection of our own national economy ... We are here to regulate," he added.
"The liberalisation policy of the government has to be complemented with stronger power for the SRA," he further said.
